Demand to strengthen the medical facilities in India.
details:
Smt. Sulata Deo: 
I, draw attention of the Government
towards the shortage of beds, doctors, and critical care facilities in
Government hospitals across the country.Premier institutions such as AIIMS
Delhi, RML Hospital, and AIIMS Bhubaneswar are overburdened with patients
coming not only from their respective cities but from neighboring States as
well. Poor and middle-class families travel long distances in the hope of
affordable treatment. However, due to limited bed capacity, shortage of specialist
doctors, and overcrowded emergency wards, many patients are forced to wait for
hours and even days for admission.This situation is? alarming. In several
cases, patients lose their lives due to delay in treatment or non-availability
of ICU beds and essential facilities. Families are left helpless, running from
one hospital to another in search of a vacant bed. Those who cannot afford
private hospitals suffer the most.The growing population and rising disease
burden demand urgent expansion of healthcare infrastructure. There is a need to
increase bed strength, fill vacant posts of doctors and paramedical staff,
upgrade district hospitals, and strengthen primary and secondary healthcare
systems to reduce pressure on tertiary institutions. ?????????? Healthcare is
not a privilege but a basic necessity. I urge the Government to take time-bound
measures to ensure strengthening the medical facilities in India.
(ENDS)

records.title: Concern over rising Cyber Fraud and Fake Call scams.
details:
Smt. Sulata Deo: I raise
a serious matter regarding the growing problem of cyber fraud and fake call scams
that are troubling people across the country and causing heavy financial
losses. Every day people are being cheated through fake bank and KYC calls,
fraudulent links, OTP scams, UPI and credit card fraud, and SIM swap frauds. A
new and dangerous trend of so-called ?online arrest? is also emerging, where
fraudsters pose as police or investigating officers, threaten people through
video calls, and force them to transfer money. Many victims lose their lifetime
savings within minutes. Senior citizens, women, students and ordinary citizens
with limited digital knowledge are the worst affected. Victims often face
difficulty in registering complaints, delays in freezing bank accounts and very
little recovery of their hard-earned money. Cybercriminals operate from
different States and even outside the country, making investigation difficult.
While digital payments and online services have grown rapidly, cyber policing,
trained manpower and public awareness have not grown at the same pace. This has
left common people vulnerable to fraud. I urge the Government to strengthen
cybercrime police units, ensure quick registration of complaints, improve
coordination with banks and telecom companies, and speed up the process of
freezing fraudulent accounts. Large-scale awareness campaigns in simple
language are also urgently needed.
(ENDS)

records.title: Demand for Metro Rail Project between Bhubaneswar and Cuttack.
details:
Smt. Sulata Deo: I draw attention of the
Government to an important matter relating to the development of Odisha ? the
need for a Metro Rail Project between Bhubaneswar and Cuttack. Bhubaneswar and
Cuttack are often called the Twin Cities of Odisha. They are major centres of
administration, education, healthcare, commerce, and employment. Every day,
lakhs of people travel between these two cities, and the number is increasing
rapidly. Due to heavy traffic on the existing roads, commuters face long
delays, pollution, and serious safety concerns. A modern Metro Rail system
between Bhubaneswar and Cuttack will greatly reduce travel time, ease traffic
congestion, and improve the overall quality of urban transport. It will also
support economic growth, attract investment, and help build a cleaner and more
sustainable environment. The population of the region is growing fast, and the
current transport infrastructure will not be able to handle future demand. A
Metro Rail network is not only desirable but essential for the long-term
development of the capital region of Odisha. I, therefore, request the Union
Government to extend full support for the early approval, funding, and
implementation of the Bhubaneswar?Cuttack Metro Rail Project. This will benefit
lakhs of commuters and contribute significantly to Odisha?s progress.
(ENDS)

records.title: Request For Resolution of Jal Jeevan Mission Issues In Odisha
details:
Smt.
Sulata Deo: A recent study in Odisha revealed that 40.55% of the surveyed
households lack access to safe drinking water. This poses serious health risks
and waterborne diseases due to contamination. Despite the State Governments
Basudha Scheme, which aims to provide clean water to both rural and urban
areas, there remains a pressing need for increased Central Assistance. The
challenges faced by Odisha in implementing the Jal Jeevan Mission deserve
compassionate attention and collaborative solutions for the well-being of its
residents. The Central Government must investigate and address the challenges
hindering the Jal Jeevan Mission in Odisha. Collaboratively, the Union and
State Governments can identify areas lacking safe water access and implement
tailored schemes. Sir, through you, I urge the Central Government to promptly
resolve these issues.
(Ends)

records.title: Demand To Increase The One Stop Centres In Odisha
details:
Smt. Sulata Deo: Violence against women persists as a
distressing issue, demanding urgent and comprehensive solutions. The One Stop
Centre (OSC) scheme, led by the Central Government, is commendable but needs
expansion in Odisha, where the number of centers is significantly lower than in
states like Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. In Odisha, the government has
established Sakhi centers to aid distressed women, yet the existing numbers
fall short of meeting the extensive demand. Expanding One Stop Centres in
Odisha is crucial to ensure comprehensive coverage and assistance for victims
of violence. Through you, Sir, I respectfully request from the Government to increase
the number of centers in Odisha to provide support to more women in the state.
(Ends)

records.title: Animal cruelty.
details:
Smt.
Sulata Deo: I
want to bring to your attention the urgent issue of cruelty against animals. Animals cannot
express their pain in human language, but they have souls and feel suffering
just like us. It is our duty to understand their problems and protect them. We
need strict laws to check cruelty against
animals and? to ensure that those who harm animals are held accountable. Proper
measures and monitoring should be implemented to prevent abuse and neglect.
Additionally, illegal slaughterhouses must be banned immediately to stop the
inhumane treatment of animals. By taking these steps, we can create a society
that respects and cares for all living beings. It is time to act and ensure
that animals are treated with the compassion and dignity they deserve.I urge
the Government to look into it.
(Ends)
